title: Over 20000 precolonial earthworks in the Southwest Amazonia.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Ran paper_context.py with --full and searched the full open-access text (PMC13558069). The data availability statement says the raw LiDAR (laser terrain scanning from aircraft) data are restricted under Brazilian law and no custom code was developed. The only Zenodo DOI in the text (10.5281/zenodo.5884351) resolves to the GDAL geospatial software library, not a dataset. The Europe PMC supplementary-files request was killed after 135 s, so the supplement could not be retrieved.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: 347 earthworks detected along 4,430 km of LiDAR flight lines (Extended Data Table 1a). Radiocarbon calibration datasets are in Supplementary Table 1a,b, and Supplementary Table 2 lists dated earthworks. The supplement is described as one combined PDF of notes, tables and figures. No downloadable table of earthwork locations or LiDAR tiles is mentioned.

a1_downloadable.note: The raw LiDAR data, which the project would need as input, are restricted under Brazilian law (stated in the paper's data availability section). The only open material is a supplementary PDF of radiocarbon tables, and I could not retrieve it.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Not checked in files. No released table of earthwork locations with labels like presence/absence or type is described, so a detection label would have to be built by hand from figures.

a3_inputs_present.note: The inputs would be LiDAR terrain rasters, which are restricted. Public substitutes such as satellite elevation models would be a different, coarser dataset.

a4_units_stated.note: Not assessable: no data table was obtained.

a5_enough_rows.note: Paper text only: 347 LiDAR-detected structures, which is under the roughly 400 needed even for classification. The '20,000' in the title is an extrapolated estimate, not observed rows.

a6_fits_laptop.note: Not assessable: the raw data are restricted.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Not assessable: no files were opened.

a8_label_provenance.note: Earthworks were identified by visual inspection of LiDAR terrain models plus field checks. That is human annotation, not a model's output.

existing_models.name: Machine-learning distribution model of Amazonian archaeological sites (PMC10069417)
existing_models.score_and_split: Not retrieved in detail; it predicts where sites occur from environmental variables.

existing_models.name: Peripato et al., Science 2023, 'More than 10,000 pre-Columbian earthworks are still hidden throughout Amazonia' (statistical distribution model built on 937 known earthworks and nine climate, soil and terrain variables)
de Souza et al., Nature Communications 2018 (MaxEnt, a presence-only distribution model, applied to earthworks on the southern rim of the Amazon)
existing_models.score_and_split: Search snippet reports AUC (area under the ROC curve) above 0.96; split not checked.

backbone.name: None from the biology backbone list. This is remote-sensing imagery, not sequences, molecules or cells.

honest_claim_h3: Not applicable. Rejected at Part A because the input data are restricted and there are too few labelled sites.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use aerial laser terrain scans of rainforest to predict where buried ancient earthworks are.
plain_idea.train_on: LiDAR terrain-model tiles from 4,430 km of flight lines, with 347 earthworks found by eye (count from the paper text only). The raw data are legally restricted.
plain_idea.predict: Whether a tile contains a geometric earthwork. The true answer comes from archaeologists inspecting the scans visually and checking in the field.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Archaeologists estimating the precolonial population of Amazonia could map sites under forest without flying new surveys. But this is archaeology, outside the biology-only scope of this project.

ml_idea: Detect earthworks in LiDAR terrain tiles, or model where earthworks occur from environmental variables. Blocked by restricted LiDAR data, only 347 observed sites, and an off-topic subject (archaeology, not biology).

effort.compute_note: Not estimated: rejected at Part A.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Read the data availability statement: raw LiDAR is restricted under Brazilian law.

verdict_reason: Archaeology, outside the biology-only scope. The raw LiDAR scans are restricted under Brazilian law (A1). The paper reports only 347 observed earthworks, not a released table (A5). The only Zenodo DOI is the GDAL software library, not data.
